text:
maya: Heads up — seeing a GPU preempt event (us-west1) but can't tie the trace in Zipkin to any logs in Loki. trace id 6a7b9f2c showing heavy queuing then preempted. Anyone seeing missing trace_id across logs?
tom: Can you paste the trace id and time window? :eyes:
sre-bot: [ALERT] gpu.preempt.count > 0 (threshold 1) in us-west1 — fired 2026-04-12T09:07:00Z — alert_id=alert-9832
maya: Trace id 6a7b9f2c, window 09:05–09:10 UTC. I ran a quick Loki query: ```{app="gpu-proxy", region="us-west1"} |= "preempt" | json | line_format "{trace_id} {msg}"``` returns nothing with that trace id. Only some entries have trace_id populated.
adrian: hmm — our trace->log correlation relies on X-Trace-Id header forwarded by the edge proxy. If proxy samples or truncates headers on retries we lose correlation. Can you run a broader Loki grep to find the short id? e.g. ```{app="gpu-proxy"} |= "6a7b"```
maya: Ran it, got matches but they are in a different pod: gpu-proxy-5d4c. Those logs have trace_id field like "6a7b9f2c-<short>" while traces are just 6a7b9f2c. Might be a formatting change from the proxy side.
nina: We shipped header-munging fix in proxy v2.3.1 last month; older pods still on v2.2.x could be adding suffixes. Can you check pod image tags for the timeframe? `kubectl get pods -n gpu -o wide --selector=app=gpu-proxy`
tom: Also check Kibana with query `trace.id:6a7b9f2c*` — Kibana supports wildcards, Loki needs explicit parse.
maya: Good call — Kibana found an application span with `trace.id:6a7b9f2c-1` at 09:06, linked to a kubelet preempt loop. But our logs ingestion pipeline strips the dash and suffix in the ingest pipeline (regex on message). Looks like two transformations fighting.
adrian: So root cause: mixed proxy versions + ingest pipeline regex that normalizes trace_id to 8 chars. We should either standardize to full UUID or keep the bare prefix. Propose changing ingest pipeline to preserve full header string and add a derived field `trace_prefix` for short-id queries.
kevin: For alerting, we should include trace_id in alert labels when present. Current alert `gpu.preempt` only has pod/node labels — add `trace_id` label from query if matched. That will make triage much faster.
nina: Agreed. Also we should tune Loki sampling: current pipeline drops trace headers on high-volume pods. I'll open a PR to stop header drop for gpu-proxy logs.
tom: Quick workaround: temporary Grafana Explore dashboard with a Logs panel using this Loki query to join by trace: ```{app=~"gpu-.*"} |= "trace" | pattern "*trace_id=*" | regexp "trace_id=(?P<tr>[^\s]+)" | tr != ""``` then filter for `tr=~"6a7b9f2c.*"`
maya: Thanks — that pulled the related logs across pods. Found correlation to a scheduling backoff on node gpu-n1 with OOM kill events ~09:04.
adrian: Ops plan: 1) nina to PR header-preserve change (owner: nina) 2) engineering to bump all gpu-proxy pods to v2.3.1 across regions (owner: kevin) 3) ops to update ingest pipeline regex to keep full trace_id + add trace_prefix (owner: adrian). ETA for rollouts?
kevin: Can run a canary today in us-west1, full rollouts tomorrow morning. I'll post the deploy plan here once scheduled. :rocket:
maya: Once canary is live I'll re-run correlation checks. For postmortem, we should add a small test that validates trace-id pass-through for logs when proxy version changes.
tom: Also adjust alert `gpu.preempt` to include `for: 2m` and add `trace_id` label merge from logs via alertmanager silence. Less noisy.
nina: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/proxy/pull/402 — preserves X-Trace-Id header, adds unit test.
adrian: thanks all. Follow-up: add a Grafana SLO card showing percentage of traces that successfully correlate to logs by 1h window (target > 98%).
maya: Noted. Will file a ticket for SLO card. :white_check_mark:
